plan-omoide.hook: Charcoal smoke and six-seat yakitori bars under the Shinjuku train tracks.
moments: Walk into the narrow alley from Shinjuku West Exit, under red lanterns and grill smoke.
Squeeze onto a stool at a counter, your coat still on, knees touching the next person.
Order negima and tsukune skewers and watch the cook turn them over the charcoal.
Drink a cold beer or a highball while trains rumble past on the tracks next to you.
Move to a second bar for one more round of skewers.
plan-omoide.tip: Look at the menu and seat charge on the door before you go in. Bars with English menus hang them outside.

plan-daikoku.hook: The world's most famous JDM car meet, inside a giant spiral of highway ramps.
moments: Drive the Shuto Expressway at night behind the guide car, the city lights passing on both sides.
Spiral down the big loop ramp into the lot and see rows of tuned cars under orange lights.
Walk past GT-Rs, Supras, RX-7s and wild bosozoku builds, and talk to owners with your phone translator.
Warm your hands with a hot can of coffee from the vending machines.
Drive back across the lit Yokohama Bay Bridge or Rainbow Bridge.
plan-daikoku.tip: Ask the owner before you photograph a car with its owner in it. Most owners are happy to open the hood if you ask.

plan-shibuya-sky.hook: An open roof 230 m above the Scramble, with Mt Fuji at sunset.
moments: Ride the dark, light-show elevator up to the 45th floor.
Step onto the open roof and feel the cold wind at the glass edge.
Look west for Mt Fuji as the sun sets behind it, about 16:55.
Lean over the corner glass and watch the Scramble crossing fill and empty far below.
Stay until dark and watch Tokyo Tower and Skytree light up.
plan-shibuya-sky.tip: Bags, hats and loose items must go in lockers before the roof. Wear a warm jacket with zip pockets.

plan-naritasan.hook: A 1,000-year-old temple with fire rituals, 10 minutes from Narita Airport.
moments: Walk up Omotesando's winding street past old wooden shops and the smell of grilled eel.
Watch the cooks at Kawatoyo cut live eels by the front window, then eat a hot unaju.
Climb the stone steps to the Great Main Hall and sit in for a goma fire ritual with big drums.
Look up at the red and green three-storey pagoda, carved with dragons.
Walk the quiet Naritasan Park behind the temple, past ponds and a waterfall.
plan-naritasan.tip: Goma rituals run about every hour in the Main Hall. Anyone can sit in for free; be there 10 minutes early.

plan-gbc-miharashi.hook: The river steps where Nina sings for Momoka in Girls Band Cry episode 2.
moments: Walk 1 km from Kawasaki West Exit to the wide concrete steps above the Tama River.
Sit on the central stairs, where Nina sings for Momoka before Momoka moves away in ep 2.
Sit bottom right of the central stairs, Nina's guitar practice spot in ep 8.
Move to bottom left, where Tomo sees Nina practise hard in ep 9, drinking-yogurt bottle next to her.
Look across the water to Tokyo while the sun sets.
plan-gbc-miharashi.tip: Bring a small bottle of drinking yogurt for the ep 9 photo. Stamp the stamp book here.

plan-gbc-minamikawara.hook: The footbridge from the opening, where Momoka runs after Nina in episode 1.
moments: Walk into the quiet streets near Nina's apartment, past small shops and houses.
Find the Nakayoshi-maru play structure in Minamikawara Park, where Momoka gives Nina her phone in ep 1.
Climb Miyakocho Footbridge, where Momoka catches up with Nina and her lost phone in ep 1.
Stand on the east side of the bridge, face toward Shitte, and match the opening shot.
Stamp the two stamp tour points.
plan-gbc-minamikawara.tip: Go in the morning when traffic is light. Step aside for residents on the bridge stairs.

plan-gbc-muza.hook: Nina's episode 1 run, a free public piano, and anime goods upstairs.
moments: Walk the 2F deck from the station to the north escalator, Nina's route searching for Momoka in ep 1.
Play the upright piano on 1F, the piano Tomo plays in a TOGENASHI TOGEARI music video.
Look at the grand piano on 2F. It is for display only.
Shop for Girls Band Cry goods at Animate Kawasaki, then get your stamp.
plan-gbc-muza.tip: The piano is free from 10:00 to 20:00. Play one short song and let the next person have a turn.

plan-gbc-lazona.hook: The mall stage where the band plays 声なき魚 in episode 3.
moments: Walk into Rufa Square, the round open-air plaza of Lazona, west of Kawasaki Station.
Stand at the Grand Stage, where Nina, Momoka and Subaru play 声なき魚 in ep 3.
Look down on the stage from the 4F and 5F walkways, the anime's angle.
Buy Girls Band Cry goods at HMV on 4F.
Eat a warm lunch in the mall before the long walk to the river.
plan-gbc-lazona.tip: The stage area is no-photo. Keep the scene in your memory, and take photos at the other spots.

plan-gbc-east-plaza.hook: Where Nina first hears Momoka play, and where the story ends.
moments: Stand in the open plaza of the East Exit, where Momoka plays a street live in ep 1.
Find Nina's view: the plaza with the station roof and the elevated deck behind.
Find the meeting place where Nina meets Hina again in ep 13.
Buy the official stamp book for ¥500 and start the stamp tour.
Come back at night to hear real street musicians.
plan-gbc-east-plaza.tip: Take the anime-angle photos in the morning. In the evening the plaza is full of people and musicians.

plan-gbc-marufuku.hook: Coffee and a thick hotcake at the table where the band plans everything.
moments: Go down to B1F of Azalea and find the stamp beside the shop door.
Ask for the second window table from the back, where Nina sits in ep 1.
Or take the 4-person table on the left, where Rupa has her plan in ep 6.
Eat a thick, hot hotcake with butter and syrup and drink a dark Marufuku coffee.
Walk to the Girls Band Cry stamp gallery in Azalea after.
plan-gbc-marufuku.tip: Go at opening or mid-afternoon to get the anime tables. Ask staff before you take photos inside.

plan-gbc-citta.hook: The live house of the band's last show in episode 13.
moments: Walk into La Cittadella, a small Italian-style street of plazas and colored walls.
Stand at the CLUB CITTA' front entrance, the final-live venue of ep 13.
Walk the alleys the band walks on its venue visit in ep 5.
Come back after dark when the street is lit.
Look for Girls Band Cry goods at Tower Records and Village Vanguard nearby.
plan-gbc-citta.tip: Check clubcitta.co.jp before you go. On show nights there is a queue at the door, so take photos early.

plan-suga.hook: The red-railed stairs of the Your Name poster and final scene.
moments: Walk 7 minutes from Yotsuya-Sanchome through quiet back streets.
Stand at the bottom of the stairs and look up: the red railing and shrine gate match the final scene.
Take the photo where Taki and Mitsuha pass each other, then turn around.
Climb to Suga Shrine and look at the Your Name ema drawings left by fans.
plan-suga.tip: Go before 09:00. Winter morning light is soft and there is no line for the same photo.

plan-shimokita.hook: Walk Kessoku Band's home streets of live houses and used-clothing shops.
moments: Step out of Shimokitazawa Station, seen in ep 4 on the day of the band photo shoot.
Browse Village Vanguard, the goods store Bocchi passes in ep 1.
Dig through used jackets and vinyl records in the small shops on the narrow streets.
Walk the Senrogai open space above the old train line, where Bocchi sits sad in ep 5.
Eat a hot curry, Shimokitazawa's famous food, to warm up.
plan-shimokita.tip: Shops open at 11:00 to 12:00. See the anime spots first while the streets are empty.

plan-shelter.hook: The real stairs down to STARRY, Bocchi's live house.
moments: Find SHELTER's narrow door and sign on the street.
Look down the stairs into the basement, as Bocchi does with Nijika in ep 1.
Take one quiet photo of the stairs from the street.
Check the show list on the door. If a band plays that night, you can buy a ticket.
plan-shelter.tip: Come on a weekday before 14:00. SHELTER asks fans not to take photos on weekend or show evenings.

plan-nakano.hook: Four floors of used figures and manga, quieter and cheaper than Akihabara.
moments: Walk the covered Sun Mall arcade from Nakano Station into the old 1960s building.
Go up to floors 2 to 4 and walk through Mandarake's many small shops.
Look at glass cases of old figures, vintage toys and rare cards.
Search the used-manga shelves for an anime artbook you like.
Eat the tall 8-layer soft-serve at Daily Chico on B1F.
plan-nakano.tip: Most shops open about 12:00. Check each glass case price tag: many rare items cost less than in Akihabara.

plan-zest.hook: The live house from Oshi no Ko episode 1, where Ai performs.
moments: Walk the Akihabara back streets to the small venue.
Stand across the street and look at the front: it matches BEAST, Ai's live venue in ep 1.
Picture baby Aqua and Ruby in the crowd, waving glow sticks for Ai.
Walk on to atre Akihabara, another ep 1 location next to the station.
plan-zest.tip: Photograph only the outside, from across the street. Do not take photos when fans queue for a show.

plan-radio-kaikan.hook: Ten floors of figures and cards in the building from Steins;Gate episode 1.
moments: Stand across the street at the Electric Town Exit and look up at the building.
Remember Steins;Gate ep 1: Okabe goes to a time-machine talk here, and a satellite crashes on the roof.
Take the elevator to the top floor, then walk down floor by floor.
Look at glass cases of figures, model kits and trading cards on every floor.
Walk the Electric Town main street past arcades and neon signs.
plan-radio-kaikan.tip: The building in the anime was replaced by a new one in 2014. Start at the top floor to avoid walking back up.

plan-kinshi.hook: The park where Chisato and Takina talk in Lycoris Recoil episode 1.
moments: Find the benches in the middle of Kinshi Park, where Chisato and Takina talk about their cafe job in ep 1.
Stand with the play equipment on both sides and the tall buildings behind, like the anime frame.
Look up at Tokyo Skytree, lit up after 17:00, above the park.
Find the Chisato and Takina manhole cover near Olinas mall, 3 minutes from the station.
plan-kinshi.tip: The manhole was set in March 2025. Photograph it from above in daylight; at night the shadows hide the art.
